• Always struggled with sitting for standardized tests.

• Look at VA schools, cost wise. Not sure what want to do at this point or what schools are good.

Elizabeth doesn't pick things up as quickly as Elayna, so she "works twice as hard for the same results" as her older sister.

She did Algebra 1 virtually, Geometry in 9th grade, and now is feeling frustrated with Algebra 2. In particular she recently struggled with a test on Quadratics.

Elizabeth currently has a B- in Algebra 2. She got an A in Algebra 1 and an A-/B in Geometry. "Has always been an A/B student"

Dad says she needs to work a little more on time management. Elayna sometimes helps Elizabeth with Algebra 2, but Elayna lacks confidence because she took Algebra 2 online. 

Family is confident Elizabeth can "pull off" the Algebra 2 course but they don't want shortcomings or gaps to then impact SAT/ACT Prep. So family would like to enroll her in tutoring soon to determine and fill in gaps (and shore up concepts like quadratics) before beginning Test Prep.

Elizabeth herself is on the fence about tutoring. Mildly open to the idea.

Elizabeth's 2022 PSAT was a 1080 with a pretty even split: she is targeting a 1250. She enjoys athletics and plays soccer, her coach estimates she could play Division 1 "wherever she wants" so Elizabeth might decide to pursue a D1 school/sports scholarship. Parents are also open to Elizabeth "going wherever she wants and doing whatever she wants to do, sports or no."

In 11th grade Elizabeth will be taking Honors Physics and Pre-Calculus.

Thank you so much for taking the time to meet with me a couple weeks ago (and apologies for how long it took to follow-up here.) AJ, I hope the fantasy football draft went well and things are off to a great start! 😄

Modifications and Next Steps
Anna had a great 2nd grade and summer with us working on her reading, and now Jen you promised her a bit of a break from Tutoring Club. You mentioned she's sometimes resistant to going to TC but always leaves happy (I was like that with all of my afterschool activities growing up. I thought I wanted to stay in my room playing video games until I got there and got involved.)
With this in mind, we'll wait until October to add Anna back to our schedule as we see how the schedule pans out and where her greatest needs are. We think she'll probably need continued support in reading and possibly math; we could likely do what we did last year where we focus on TC Reading but work on math homework with her on an ad hoc basis as she brings it in.
Meeting Summary
Jen, you said Anna is happy to be back at school and is off to a great start for 3rd grade at Jamestown. She is engaged with her friends and active in activities (biking, trampolining, softball, soccer, gymnastics, and tennis).
She will likely continue to get extra reading and math support at school, and you're looking into a psych evaluation around the end of October (to address the possibility of anxiety, ADHD, a processing gap, and/or providing her with a 504.) As all of those steps come together, please keep us in the loop so we can make sure we're matching and meeting Anna's needs as best as possible.
Anna is a very organized, checklist-oriented, by the book person. You mentioned she might organize the art cabinet in her free time, or assemble Legos by following the exact instructions.
I wonder if this "following the rules" basis is also what appeals to her about team sports. Jen, you said Anna will get moody or withdrawn if she's playing inside for too long. So continuing to engage her physically outside with activities that have clear rules and objectives for her to follow is a good mix.
Anna doesn't avoid homework, but she doesn't like to do it alone. Similarly, she is prone to the occasional outburst or metldown which has led to her staying home from school, missing camp, or (in the spring) missing TC. We did note this doesn't tend to happen with activities that are active, so she may be dreading the brainwork or 'sitting still' part of these things.

I'm in full support of a little TC break for Anna, but am also eager to welcome her back to be sure we can help boost her confident and keep her foundations in math, reading, and writing stronger. There's a key mix to addressing both strong academic foundations and social-emotional regulation, and we want Anna to feel happy and confident in all areas as she continues to explore 8-and-9-and-10 year old feelings 😄

As always, the door is open if/when you need me (phone, email, or Zoom 😄)

September 16 Meeting Summary:
Hi Katie and Mike,

Thanks for meeting with me a couple weeks ago (and many apologies for how long the turnaround took on Alexander's reading test and follow-up from that meeting.)

Recommendation
Based on Alexander's current Reading and Writing levels, my recommendation is to continue with TC Writing with TC Reading Vocabulary exercises built into each session. Usually students in this hybrid spend about 10 minutes on vocab in each session, including reading short passages and applying and inferring new words, and then utilise the new vocab in their writing. More details and explanation below.

Passing Level B!
Hopefully Alexander showed you his Writing Level B certificate last week 😄 I was so proud of him for passing our grammar post-test on his first try (for many of our students they need two tries at that) and the wonderful final compositions he worked on (the end of Level B focuses on friendly letter writing and formatting.0

Progress Reports and Reading Results
I've attached to this email Alexander's Writing progress report (updated since our meeting) and a reading progress report based on the assessment he took in his 9/20 session. Because Alexander is approximately "on grade level" in Writing we'd discussed possibly shifting to TC Reading as Reading is an essential aid to writing, and Alexander remains very resistant to reading at home.

I've attached Alexander's Reading report from September and from his initial assessment with Katherine in May. Comparing the two, we see a very small regression in reading comprehension (likely summer slide, or just an off/tired day.) What surprises me the most is the much larger regression in Reading Vocabulary. As we've discussed, Alexander is an extremely bright young man and I have no doubt his high comprehension score is very accurate.

Lacking the precise and sophisticated-enough vocabulary to express himself came up as a concern in our meeting, and I think we see this reflected in the vocab results. While Alexander's vocab might not have truly slid 'back' that far, I believe continuing to work on TC Writing and building in Vocab support will allow him the best chance to succeed at increasing critical thought, self-confidence, introspection, and arming him with the right words to express himself.



I know you have a meeting coming up with Katherine to discuss tuition (hence my late night email and quick summary.) She can go over the progress report in more detail with you if needed.

Every time I've seen Alexander the past few weeks I've thought about that page from Back 2 School Night full of question marks for his favourite things, and how Michael so aptly described him as "a loveable puzzle." (This also came to mind when Alexander dove head-first into the passenger seat of the car through the open window a week or two ago 😄)

Alexander has plenty of personality, plenty of thoughts, and plenty of opinions and preferences (it's clear in how he comes out of his shell with tutors and students, in the flickers of pride I see when he's working on writing, and even in the fierce opposition he puts up at home to reading, or the anxiety he associates with TV/film and difficult conflict.) Alexander is processing a lot of feelings, and I look forward to continuing to work with him this fall to be able to give him the right words and language to express all that is going on in his head.

As always, the door is open if/when you need me (phone, email, or Zoom 😄)

Email to parents 7/7/22:
Hi, Vivia and Calvin.

It was a pleasure meeting with you last night to review Caden’s assessment results and your writing goals for him! Did you have any further questions for me? As I mentioned in our meeting, I was very impressed with Caden’s work ethic and maturity when we met 😊

We look forward to working with Caden for his four trial hours and I look forward to reconnecting with you on Wednesday, 7/20, at 3p. You should have received a calendar invite for that so please let me know if you did not. Welcome to the TC Family!

As promised, attached are the results of his assessment and the documents that you signed, as well as the link to the weekly health screening questionnaire that you will need to complete by noon this Saturday, please. Please ensure that you complete that on time so that Caden can attend his sessions next week.

1.	Link to the In-person Health Screening Questionnaire for you to complete (one per student).

Sam will circle back with you on scheduling options for next week. By way of this email, I’m looping in the rest of the team. 

Sam, Caden is rising 8th and will have four trial hours from meeting us at McLean Day. He is available next week (week of 7/11), Monday through Friday, 10am-1pm. They would like one hour sessions and prefer the 10am slot, if available. He will be doing TC Writing Level G, with some modifications. Can you please start a BC task and tag me so we can discuss? I’d love for him to work with Grace but forgot that she comes in later. Perhaps noon is open and that would work for them?

Grace, over those four sessions, his parents would like to see how he responds to tutoring since this format will be new to him. As I mentioned, he’s a very strong student who just needs some writing support. The goals that they listed on his family information form are, “Improve writing skills, grammar, vocabulary to prepare Caden for the future and for standardized tests.” His parents would also like to see some work samples. Level G is all about advanced grammar and punctuation skills to help him to develop more sophisticated sentence structure. While those do not include writing samples per se, his parents are okay with sending home some composition homework. Can you please pull together some things for his tutor(s)?

Caden wants to apply to TJHSST this season for admissions his Freshman year so his parents would like to make sure that he will be ready for the essay portion of the application. To help with that, he should get through Level G and through the expository writing skills in Level I. That Level I will also be the most practical and useful for late middle school and high school writing. Their hope is that Caden will acclimate well to TC and then continue with us to help him prep for the admissions process and higher level writing assignments.

I think that’s it for now. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Thank you, all, and enjoy the rest of your day!

Wyatt is a female. 
-1st grade was a very challenging/ struggle year.
-all of K parents moved her to a private Kindergarten to mitigate learning loss/ avoid online at APS
-1st grade was her first year at Jamestown ES.
-Note: family did apply to several private schools after K (Congressional, Langley, Potomac) 
-her WISP intelligence test/ testing done for private schools indicated she is "near gifted" and highly intelligent, but the testing and the neuropsych eval said she "disengages when bored" -- potential there but doesn't apply
-1/2 way through 1st grade year = ADHD diagnosis
-parents / school had concerns about her focus, attention, and not finishing work on time
-she received reading intervention throughout all of 1st grade year
-2x/ week pullout reading group
-dad thinks it was OG method used
-socially = dad said she does very well

Primary concern: 
-reading!
-point of contention at home
-at home will not read voluntarily 
-dad implemented a reward system for her reading -- incentives, huge buy in for her
-in terms of what she's currently reading: "The Bad Guys" series (dad bought all of them but she mostly has him read to her
-"Princess in Black" series -- can read 2-3 chapters but needs help with multi-syllable words
-still flips her b/d
-reversal of some letters, numbers
-chunking: excellent and can break down words but struggles to smoothly/ fluently but those words together


-no IEP or 504 in place (school determined not needed at this time)
-KC asked dad about "best time of day"/ if she's on any meds
-small dose of Riddalin for ADHD
-most focused after she takes meds (usually 8a) but teacher noted by mid-day/ afternoon wore off
-family experimenting with the longer release tablets this summer

-asked if morning sessions would be best for her, but she's in a day camp from 8:30a- 4:30p all week right now
-Saturdays might be a great morning option! 
-has never had tutoring in past

-other notes: dad works for Amazon Web Services (AWS) and will be in NY this entire week for a work conference. Very very eager/ ready to start immediately!!

(from homeroom teacher Jackie Laurenzi)
Hi Caroline and Grace, 

Ms. Talbot passed along your message that you would like some information about Hudson's reading progress so far this year. 

First, I just want to let you know what a diligent, positive student Hudson is in reading class. He participates, partners well with his classmates for book talks, and asks questions when he needs to. 

Hudson ended last year approaching the benchmark for the end of 2nd grade. I began testing him (using our Fountas and Pinnell assessment tool) at a similar level to start the school year. He has been successful in reading more challenging texts, both with his fluency and comprehension, and he is ready to test again at a level that is slightly above the benchmark for where we are at this point in 3rd grade. So basically, Hudson has grown enormously as a capable reader since the end of last year. 

Hudson just took his Unit 1 post-assessment in reading class. He did very well in his skills having to do with Inferring and Predicting. His work on Summarizing was challenging. Husdon did a great job of saying what lesson the character learned but left out a synopsis of the story overall. He will bring his assessment home to go over with parents this weekend, so you will be able to see what I mean. 

I have invited Hudson to be part of our Read Naturally Live group, so he can continue to strengthen his fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension skills. The passages and work he will do are consistent with his current reading abilities. 

Please let me know if you have any other questions or more specific information you would like.

column247:
From 2/16/21 8:30p call w/MSS and Lynn:
1.	Max Todorov is an 8th grader at LMS, not in AAP, but HNs (as per LMS classes).
2.	He just turned 14 last week – Happy Birthday, Max! 
3.	Max is friends with Colin Blakley ?
4.	Online is not working for Max, but fortunately he is returning to in-person hybrid on 3/2.
5.	He has a recent ADD diagnosis (Oct/Sept), and is embarking on treatments now.  His EF skills are weak. Max is their third child, but the first with these issues. Parents recognize that they are normally spotty at this age, but his ADD is exacerbating it.
a.	He also has some LDs. 
1.	Written expression since 5th grade.
2.	Reading was below average.
b.	Recommendations from report included “Continue tutoring for writing and math, as needed. Graphic organizers. Dragon speak.”
6.	His teachers lay out his classwork on G Classroom on Mondays and has a week to get it done. They also put out slides for the day.
7.	He’s falling down in class because he’s not attending to it and not completing work when he should. He then needs to complete for homework, which is more to keep track of 
8.	When asked how his confidence is, his mom replied “defensive.”
9.	He is receiving A/Bs with a lot of structural support. No penalties for late work this year. Grades not been too big a problem. Was doing much better when in school prior to pandemic. Trouble staying on right path for class.
10.	He is easily distracted during the school day so his mom holds onto his phone, and they learned how to block YouTube videos.
11.	When asked if he’s struggling with any content areas, his mom reported that it’s hard to tell if content areas are at play or just attention span. He doesn’t connect the dots or have the drive to pull it together. Not doing independently – and not listening to mom.
12.	Mom reports that his teachers like him, he’s easy going, not a trouble maker/disruptive; polite, kind; performance is hot/cold in same class depending on the day.
13.	Max is open to tutoring. Previously, he worked with an in-home tutor (a retired ES teacher in neighborhood) but outgrew her. In the beginning of year, he did online tutoring for math and science through the Fusion School. Mom reports that it was okay; he liked his tutor and did get his work done. Not great in terms of he didn’t work on his own – claimed connection difficulties or something else. Mom suggested online homework club tonight but he was adamant against it. Then mentioned that Colin was coming in-person (mom didn’t know there were in-person options out there ?).
14.	Goals:
a.	Help him learn how to keep on track. He needs help organizing what needs to be done.
b.	Then needs help getting started.
c.	Also, how to manage the technology of it. In the assignment – how navigate back and forth.
15.	Scheduling:
a.	In-person only. I did discuss limited availability but I saw some pockets. 
b.	Gets out at 2p TU-FR. Will be in school TH/FR.
c.	Mondays are a good day – completely free.
d.	Plays baseball with Colin Wednesday evenings at 8p.
16.	Initial Recommendations:
a.	I recommended that Max meet with Katherine first but mom was concerned she may not get enough out of him to understand what’s needed since he often just says everything is fine. 
b.	I also recommended an assessment to review the reading and writing but she was afraid we’d get push back jumping right into an assessment since he had his other testing last fall. 
c.	As such, I recommended that we start with a trial session ($64) so that Sam can work with him for an hour then share his initial insights and recommendations with Katherine.
d.	Based on initial conversations, I thought the traditional path may work, of two hours a day, 4-5 days a week. Or one hour a day and RAMP to start. The trial session and game plan meeting will flesh that out more.
17.	Lynn Todorov, 1946 Macarthur Drive, McLean, VA 22101, lstodorov@aol.com, 229-506-1047

The conversation was about scheduling a tutoring session for a student struggling with calculus at Langley High School. The outcome was an agreement to schedule a trial tutoring hour for the student.
Recap
The parent expressed concern about their daughter, a junior at Langley High, struggling with calculus and needing a tutor familiar with the school's grading system.

The daughter has been referred to an internal tutoring center at Langley but is not interested in that option, prompting the parent to seek external tutoring services.
Michelle Scott, the owner of the Tutoring Club, explained the tutoring process, including an initial trial session to assess the student's needs and abilities, which costs $65.
The parent was informed that the average cost for ongoing tutoring would be between $450 to $550 per month, with a one-time registration fee of $999 and no long-term contracts required.
The parent agreed to schedule a trial hour for the daughter, preferring it to be online, and discussed potential scheduling options for the following week after the daughter returns from a tournament.
Tasks
The parent will schedule a trial tutoring hour for their daughter with the Tutoring Club, preferably for next week after discussing with her.

column246:
TLC August 26 2022
Next Steps and Modifications
Thank you for submitting your school year scheduling preferences so promptly. We have Ian on the schedule this year for four hours a week. As we discussed today, we'll stick to two hours of TC Writing and two hours of TC Math a week. Ian's schedule will be Wed / Sat starting the week of 8/29.
You mentioned concern that Ian might be resistant, reluctant, or stubborn for Saturday tutoring. With this in mind, I'll see if we can add extra breaks or game incentives and let tutors know to be patient with Ian on Saturdays and take it easy as necessary. I will let you know if Saturday ends up being any concern on our end or if things go poorly.
Per your request, we can let Ian check out a laptop from us to type his compositions. This will be a great incentive for him and excellent practice in responsibility (if students are distracted or drawn to games or not working well, we take the laptop away.)
I've attached Ian's progress reports to this email, including his reading progress report from his initial assessment. You'll notice his reading is on grade level right now which is why we're focusing more on Writing and Math right now.
Ian prefers working with young, male tutors and someone with fun / engaging / upbeat personalities. As I mentioned I can't guarantee tutors but we will update our pairing notes to put Ian at tables matching his preferences whenever possible. 

Meeting Summary
Ian has had a great start to TC this summer. He's attended 27 hours so far splitting Writing and Math (plus a couple weeks at 6 hrs/week where we added in Reading.)
He's going into 5th grade at Cardinal Elementary and overall has mixed feelings. School and teachers aren't concerned with Ian's progress right now, but we agree that this will be an important time to develop and solidify foundations in order to keep middle and high school approachable, manageable, and fun for him. We also want to increase his stamina, and he's done well with two hour tutoring sessions so I can't wait to see how that continues to improve.
Ian's doctor has reported "huge progress" with his Convergence Inconsistency. I am so glad to hear that, and I hope things continue to improve.
You mentioned he feels confident in (this is reflected in the very quick progress he's made in our math curriculum!) but feels overwhelmed by writing. He's also a strong reader but gravitates toward comics and goofy / lighter stories. You might consider the following books or comics 
Percy Jackson and the Olympians
Ian is at a prime age to start reading this series and I can confirm it's light-hearted and has a silly aspect to it (the first Chapter title of book 1 is "I accidentally vaporized my pre-algebra teacher")
If Ian likes this, he may also like Rick Riordan's other series The Kane Chronicles as they have that same positive / goofy humour in an action-packed fantasy adventure
The Septimus Heap Series
Coraline
Overall this has a darker mood, but the writing is sophisticated and the plot / symbolism advanced so might engage Ian more than the younger content he's reading.
This Spider-Man comic is rated T for Teen (there are some lewd references and mentions of drug use) but I've been reading it the past couple weeks and I've found it incorporates very sophisticated vocabulary and a wonderful message while also making me giggle with all the farse and artistic silliness that comic books entail.
But I really like all things Spider-Man so I suspect I'm rather biased on that front
I know Ian likes Pokémon, so the original Pokémon Adventures manga might interest him. These books are easy to read in terms of comprehension but I've found re-reading them over the years that they incorporate some more advanced vocabulary words and very articulate, thoughtful, and moving themes. Plus all the fun, laughter, and adventure of a visual Pokémon adventure.
This is a blast from the past (at least for me) but Ian might also enjoy the Animorphs series about teenagers who can transform into different animals. As you mentioned Ian likes animals, I love this series because whenever the teenagers interact with a new animal it includes lots of fun facts and scientific accuracies about them.
Our tutors really enjoy working with Ian. He has great sessions for both Math and Writing and has made a lot of progress in drafting, syntax, and grammar fluency. I've attached a scan of his first written essay to this email for you, and showed you the difference between this revised draft and his rough draft in-center. Ian's behaviour in center is generally good though we occasionally have days where he's low energy or easily distracted.
Our goals for Ian in the coming semester are to increase his confidence and overcome learned helplessness. You mentioned when Ian feels stuck or like he's behind he'll fail to ask for help, so we want him to advocate for himself more. TLC August 26 2022
Next Steps and Modifications
Thank you for submitting your school year scheduling preferences so promptly. We have Ian on the schedule this year for four hours a week. As we discussed today, we'll stick to two hours of TC Writing and two hours of TC Math a week. Ian's schedule will be Wed / Sat starting the week of 8/29.
You mentioned concern that Ian might be resistant, reluctant, or stubborn for Saturday tutoring. With this in mind, I'll see if we can add extra breaks or game incentives and let tutors know to be patient with Ian on Saturdays and take it easy as necessary. I will let you know if Saturday ends up being any concern on our end or if things go poorly.
Per your request, we can let Ian check out a laptop from us to type his compositions. This will be a great incentive for him and excellent practice in responsibility (if students are distracted or drawn to games or not working well, we take the laptop away.)
I've attached Ian's progress reports to this email, including his reading progress report from his initial assessment. You'll notice his reading is on grade level right now which is why we're focusing more on Writing and Math right now.
Ian prefers working with young, male tutors and someone with fun / engaging / upbeat personalities. As I mentioned I can't guarantee tutors but we will update our pairing notes to put Ian at tables matching his preferences whenever possible. 

Meeting Summary
Ian has had a great start to TC this summer. He's attended 27 hours so far splitting Writing and Math (plus a couple weeks at 6 hrs/week where we added in Reading.)
He's going into 5th grade at Cardinal Elementary and overall has mixed feelings. School and teachers aren't concerned with Ian's progress right now, but we agree that this will be an important time to develop and solidify foundations in order to keep middle and high school approachable, manageable, and fun for him. We also want to increase his stamina, and he's done well with two hour tutoring sessions so I can't wait to see how that continues to improve.
Ian's doctor has reported "huge progress" with his Convergence Inconsistency. I am so glad to hear that, and I hope things continue to improve.
You mentioned he feels confident in (this is reflected in the very quick progress he's made in our math curriculum!) but feels overwhelmed by writing. He's also a strong reader but gravitates toward comics and goofy / lighter stories. You might consider the following books or comics 
Percy Jackson and the Olympians
Ian is at a prime age to start reading this series and I can confirm it's light-hearted and has a silly aspect to it (the first Chapter title of book 1 is "I accidentally vaporized my pre-algebra teacher")
If Ian likes this, he may also like Rick Riordan's other series The Kane Chronicles as they have that same positive / goofy humour in an action-packed fantasy adventure
The Septimus Heap Series
Coraline
Overall this has a darker mood, but the writing is sophisticated and the plot / symbolism advanced so might engage Ian more than the younger content he's reading.
This Spider-Man comic is rated T for Teen (there are some lewd references and mentions of drug use) but I've been reading it the past couple weeks and I've found it incorporates very sophisticated vocabulary and a wonderful message while also making me giggle with all the farse and artistic silliness that comic books entail.
But I really like all things Spider-Man so I suspect I'm rather biased on that front
I know Ian likes Pokémon, so the original Pokémon Adventures manga might interest him. These books are easy to read in terms of comprehension but I've found re-reading them over the years that they incorporate some more advanced vocabulary words and very articulate, thoughtful, and moving themes. Plus all the fun, laughter, and adventure of a visual Pokémon adventure.
This is a blast from the past (at least for me) but Ian might also enjoy the Animorphs series about teenagers who can transform into different animals. As you mentioned Ian likes animals, I love this series because whenever the teenagers interact with a new animal it includes lots of fun facts and scientific accuracies about them.
Our tutors really enjoy working with Ian. He has great sessions for both Math and Writing and has made a lot of progress in drafting, syntax, and grammar fluency. I've attached a scan of his first written essay to this email for you, and showed you the difference between this revised draft and his rough draft in-center. Ian's behaviour in center is generally good though we occasionally have days where he's low energy or easily distracted.
Our goals for Ian in the coming semester are to increase his confidence and overcome learned helplessness. You mentioned when Ian feels stuck or like he's behind he'll fail to ask for help, so we want him to advocate for himself more. We also specifically want to shoot for Advanced Math placement for middle school. The school will assess readiness in January, and you will share the results with me of his initial Math assessment in September so we can see what he most needs to work on.
For math specifically, you mentioned that Ian sometimes doesn't parse all of a word problem. So he'll look just for the numbers and not actually read the question. In math sessions we can encourage him to slow down and incorporate word problems practice related to the concepts he's learning with us.
